heading: Pressure acts most dramatically on gas
narration: Ocean pressure rises by roughly one atmosphere for every 10 meters of seawater.

args.caption: One additional atmosphere for every 10 metres of seawater

heading: Pressure acts most dramatically on gas
narration: Air compresses strongly under that load; liquid water does not compress nearly as much.

heading: Pressure acts most dramatically on gas
narration: Animals with lungs or large gas spaces face a serious mechanical problem.

heading: Pressure acts most dramatically on gas
narration: Many permanent deep-sea residents instead have water-rich tissues and no large internal air cavity.

heading: They are built for one pressure regime
narration: Deep-sea animals are not simply pressure-proof versions of shallow animals. Their membranes, enzymes, circulation and behavior function as a coordinated system under their normal conditions.

heading: They are built for one pressure regime
narration: That is why an animal thriving at 2,000 meters may be stressed when brought to the surface even if it is not visibly crushed.

heading: They are built for one pressure regime
narration: Pressure changes chemical reaction rates, and rapid decompression can disrupt normal physiology.

heading: Vertical migrants tolerate large daily changes
narration: Some midwater species move hundreds of meters each night and return to depth by day.

args.caption: Pressure change during nightly migration, without apparent harm

heading: Vertical migrants tolerate large daily changes
narration: NOAA notes that certain species experience pressure changes equivalent to about 100 atmospheres during these migrations without apparent harm.

heading: Vertical migrants tolerate large daily changes
narration: Their tolerance does not mean every deep-sea species can make the same trip. Depth range is species-specific.

args.caption: Pressure change during nightly migration, without apparent harm

heading: Why humans and submersibles need protection
narration: Humans depend on gas-filled lungs and cannot expose the body directly to deep-ocean pressure.

heading: Why humans and submersibles need protection
narration: Submersibles keep occupants near surface pressure inside a rigid pressure hull. Cameras and electronics also need pressure housings or oil-filled designs because air-filled components can collapse.

heading: Common myths and questions
narration: A common question is: Why are deep-sea fish not flattened? Their internal pressure is close to the surrounding water pressure, and many lack large compressible gas spaces.

args.term: WHY DEEP-SEA FISH ARE NOT FLATTENED
includes: Internal pressure close to the surrounding water pressure

heading: Common myths and questions
narration: Some vertical migrants can visit shallower water. Many permanent deep residents cannot tolerate the combined changes in pressure, temperature, light and water chemistry.

heading: Common myths and questions
narration: A common question is: Does pressure increase at a constant rate? A useful approximation is one additional atmosphere for every 10 meters of seawater, although density and local conditions create small differences.

args.caption: One additional atmosphere of seawater, as a useful approximation

heading: Common myths and questions
narration: A common question is: Are gelatinous bodies weak? They may be delicate during collection, but in their normal environment a water-rich body can be efficient and well matched to high pressure.

excludes: Weak, though it may be delicate during collection

heading: The balloon test
narration: Picture two objects descending together: a sealed balloon and a water-filled bag.

heading: The balloon test
narration: The balloon changes dramatically because gas compresses. The water-filled bag changes much less.

heading: The balloon test
narration: That is not a complete model of an animal, but it explains why lungs and gas-filled swim bladders are such important pressure problems.

heading: The balloon test
narration: Deep species still need proteins, membranes, enzymes, and nervous systems that function under high pressure.

heading: The balloon test
narration: They are not immune. They are adapted to a pressure regime. Bring some of them to the surface too quickly and the chemistry, temperature, and tissues can fail even when there is no dramatic crushing event.

heading: What pressure actually changes
narration: Pressure is not one problem with one solution. It changes gas volume, chemical reactions, protein shape, membrane behavior, buoyancy, and the engineering required to observe an animal.

args.title: WHAT PRESSURE CHANGES

heading: What pressure actually changes
narration: That is why a deep species cannot be summarized as simply 'strong enough' to resist the water.

narration: A balloon, syringe, or crushed container can demonstrate gas compression, but it cannot reproduce the molecular biology of a living deep-sea animal.

heading: The three-part answer
narration: Chemically, maintain proteins and membranes that work under the local pressure. Ecologically, remain within the depth and temperature range the species is adapted to.

heading: The three-part answer

heading: What to notice in the edit
narration: The edit should alternate between the pressure scale and examples of body design: a human lung, a gas bladder, a water-rich gelatinous animal, and a rigid submersible pressure sphere.

heading: What to notice in the edit
narration: That contrast keeps the explanation physical. It also prevents the common mistake of using a dramatic implosion animation as if every deep animal were an air-filled machine.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: The phrase 'water is incompressible' is a useful simplification, not a claim that pressure has no biological effect.

args.boundary: Not a claim that pressure has no biological effect

heading: Evidence limit
narration: NOAA notes that pressure changes chemical reaction rates and that pressure-adapted animals can develop metabolic problems at the surface.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: Some vertical migrants also tolerate large daily pressure changes, but that does not mean every permanent deep resident can move freely between the surface and the abyss.

heading: Closing
narration: Deep-sea animals survive pressure by being built for it from the molecule up, not by wearing invisible armor.

args.label: AS THE WATER ABOVE GETS HEAVIER

heading: Closing
narration: The cleanest clue is what they do not carry: large gas spaces that would behave very differently as the water above them gets heavier.
